title: A Quickstart Guide to Positioning (15 March 2021)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The five components of positioning (competitive alternatives, differentiated capabilities, value, target customers, market category), the order to work them in, the status quo as a common alternative, warnings about phantom competitors and about creating a new category.

title: Books (Obviously Awesome and Sales Pitch)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Obviously Awesome sets out a step-by-step positioning process for B2B technology companies; Sales Pitch builds an eight-step pitch structure on the same concepts.

title: What is Demand-Side Sales? (undated, posted by Bob)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Buying starts with a struggle; the four forces (push, pull, anxiety, habit) are named; the six-phase buying timeline (first thought, passive looking, active looking, deciding, onboarding, ongoing use); interviews with real buyers rather than personas.

title: Van Westendorp Pricing (the Price Sensitivity Meter)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The four Van Westendorp questions, origin in the 1970s, the 1993 purchase-intent extension, and its limits: no competitive context, weak theory behind the line crossings, no volume prediction without the extension; best suited to new-to-market products.

title: Comparison Tables for Products, Services, and Features (9 February 2024)
publisher: Nielsen Norman Group (Kate Moran and Taylor Dykes)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. When comparison tables help, keeping to about five items or fewer, consistent values for every attribute as the biggest problem, a way to highlight differences, plain labels, options as columns and attributes as rows, mobile trade-offs.

title: How Online Reviews Influence Sales (page dated 4 December 2025; findings first published 2017)
publisher: Spiegel Research Center, Medill, Northwestern University
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A product with five reviews had a 270% greater purchase likelihood than one with none; diminishing returns after five; bigger effect for higher-priced products; purchase likelihood peaked at 4.0 to 4.7 stars; verified buyer badge raised odds of purchase by 15%.

title: Write high quality reviews
supports: Opened with WebFetch (no last-updated date shown). Google's guidance for review and comparison content: evidence and first-hand experience, quantitative measures, what sets a product apart from competitors, comparable options and who each suits, pros and cons, quality over length.

title: FTC Policy Statement Regarding Advertising Substantiation (23 November 1984)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A reasonable basis is required for objective claims, express and implied, before they run; the factors that set the level of proof; establishment claims such as 'tests prove' need at least that level of support.

title: Statement of Policy Regarding Comparative Advertising (13 August 1979)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The FTC encourages truthful comparisons that name competitors, with the basis of comparison clear; comparative ads are judged like other ads; truthful, non-deceptive disparagement is allowed; industry codes demanding more proof for comparative claims are inappropriate.

title: Advertising FAQ's: A Guide for Small Business (April 2001, edited January 2025)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Comparative advertising is legal if truthful; objective evidence before the ad runs; proof for express and implied claims; fine print cannot fix a misleading main claim and qualifiers sit close to the claim; testimonials rarely substantiate objective claims; ad agencies can be liable.

title: FTC's Endorsement Guides: What People Are Asking
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Material connections must be disclosed clearly in the endorsement itself; employees disclose their employer; testimonials showing unusual results need a disclosure of what people generally get; guides revised in 2023.

title: 15 U.S. Code 1125: False designations of origin, false descriptions, and dilution forbidden
publisher: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Section 1125(a)(1)(B) (Lanham Act section 43(a)) makes a party liable for misrepresenting its own or another's goods or services in commercial advertising, and lets anyone likely to be damaged bring a civil action. Statute text hosted by Cornell LII.

title: National Advertising Division
supports: Opened with WebFetch. NAD is an industry self-regulatory body (since 1971) that reviews national advertising for truth and accuracy; any company, including a competitor, can file a challenge; refusals to comply are referred to the FTC; the Fast-Track SWIFT track targets decisions within 20 business days; filing fees apply.

title: CAP Code, Section 3: Misleading advertising
publisher: Advertising Standards Authority / Committee of Advertising Practice (UK)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Rule 3.7 documentary evidence before publishing objective claims; 3.2 obvious exaggeration; comparisons with identifiable competitors (same needs, objective comparison of material, relevant, verifiable and representative features, no confusion); price comparisons; no denigration or unfair use of a rival's reputation; rules on 'free'; unqualified superlatives treated as comparisons with every rival.

title: ASA Ruling on LanguageNut Ltd (20 August 2025)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Competitor Sanako UK challenged a comparison blog post on LanguageNut's own website; claims on content, ease of use and price were unsubstantiated and not verifiable; complaint upheld.

title: ASA Ruling on Vodafone Ltd (18 September 2024)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. BT challenged TV, X and web ads claiming 'the same broadband' as BT for less and that millions of BT customers were switching; small print not clearly linked, the Ofcom report did not support the claim, no evidence for 'millions'; upheld.

title: ASA Ruling on Nectar Sleep Ltd (12 August 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Simba Sleep challenged a 'Save up to 65%' homepage claim measured against an average of other brands' prices; the basis was unclear, an average is not a price anyone can pay, and the figure exaggerated savings; upheld.

title: Marketing and advertising: the law, Regulations that affect advertising
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Advertising to businesses falls under the Business Protection from Misleading Marketing Regulations 2008 (no misleading comparisons, care with rivals' logos and trade marks); consumer advertising under the DMCC Act unfair practices rules; enforcement penalties up to 300,000 pounds or 10% of global turnover, whichever is higher.

title: Misleading and comparative advertising directive
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The directive covers misleading advertising between businesses; its comparative advertising rules also apply to advertising aimed at consumers and fully harmonise the conditions under which comparisons are allowed across EU countries.

title: Unfair Commercial Practices Directive
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Directive 2005/29/EC on unfair B2C practices; Directive (EU) 2019/2161 applies from 28 May 2022; Commission guidance notice of 17 December 2021 covers reviews, endorsements, dark patterns and more; Directive (EU) 2024/825 on empowering consumers for the green transition applies from 27 September 2026.

title: Unfair pricing (Your Europe; last checked 30 April 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. A price reduction must show the lowest price of the previous 30 days; quoted prices include taxes and delivery charges; 'free' may only cost the response, collection or delivery; traders must say when a price is personalised by automated decision-making.

title: Federal Trade Commission Announces Bipartisan Rule Banning Junk Ticket and Hotel Fees (17 December 2024)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The Rule on Unfair or Deceptive Fees covers live-event tickets and short-term lodging: total price with mandatory fees shown most prominently; effective 12 May 2025 per the linked release; other industries remain under general deception law.

title: Providing clear and accurate information about prices: summary (CMA209; published 18 November 2025, updated 7 January 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. The total price, including unavoidable fees and taxes, must be given up front; hiding mandatory charges until later (drip pricing) is illegal; 'from' prices must include mandatory charges; subscription price display; penalties up to 10% of turnover or 300,000 pounds.

title: Online retailers: including mandatory delivery fees in the total price (2 November 2026)
supports: Opened with WebFetch. CMA open letter reminding UK online retailers that mandatory delivery fees must be included in the total price and shown up front, pointing to CMA209.

title: Product Hunt Launch Guide
supports: Opened with WebFetch. Launching at 12:01 a.m. Pacific Time is suggested; company accounts are not allowed; makers may hunt their own product; you may share a launch but may not ask people directly to upvote; relaunch after significant new iterations; Product Hunt is free.
